html:
Hatuey was a Taino chief from Hispaniola who fled to eastern Cuba to warn its people about the Spanish and led them against Diego Velazquez's conquest of the island in 1511. Captured, he was burned alive in 1512.

Las Casas, who was with the Spanish in Cuba, told how a friar offered Hatuey baptism so that he could go to heaven. Hatuey asked if Spaniards went there too, and on hearing yes, said he would rather not go where he would meet such cruel people.

Velazquez completed the conquest and founded towns including Havana and Santiago. Within decades most of Cuba's Taino had died. Cubans call Hatuey the first rebel of the Americas.
